Process: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) grown in a fed-batch bioreactor. Biomass concentration x1 and substrate (glucose) concentration x2 are measured every hour, in g/L. The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

answer.feedback: C9 fits within the noise and all four parameters are estimated precisely. It has the highest Akaike weight (0.731), so it is preferred over C40. C40 gives essentially the same fit, but its Ki runs to infinity, reducing the Andrews law to a simpler form; this does not justify preferring the more complex candidate.
answer.reasoning: C9 meets the acceptance criteria: chi2 116.9 is below the 95% limit of 148.8, and every parameter has t > 1. C40 also fits, but has a lower Akaike weight and an unbounded Ki estimate. C8 is rejected for substantial lack of fit.
